record.paper_title: Measurement of Energy Spectrum and Elemental Composition of PeV Cosmic Rays: Open Problems and Prospects
record.original_question: How can air-shower-array analyses reconstruct primary cosmic-ray energy and mass composition in a way that is not merely a model-dependent consistency check, given the intrinsic degeneracy among primary energy, primary mass, and hadronic-interaction modeling, the lack of direct mass observables for most arrays, and shower-to-shower fluctuations?

evidence.quote: In fact, analysis of shower data consists in the disentanglement of a threefold problem involving primary energy, primary mass and modelling of hadronic interactions (for a discussion about hadronic interactions in CR physics see, as an example, refs. [47,48] and references therein).
Strictly speaking, when operating with shower arrays there are no observables directly related to the mass of the primary particle, and its measurement is very indirect.

Therefore, a typical data analysis consists in finding a combination of primary energy spectrum, elemental composition and hadronic interaction characteristics to obtain a consistent description of the experimental results. Clearly, this is not a measurement, but only a consistency check of some trial models. In case of discrepancy, it is difficult to identify the origin; in case of agreement, is the parameter combination unique?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a ground-based air-shower array that detects extensive atmospheric cascades initiated by primary cosmic rays. For each event the array records a set of observables O (e.g. lateral particle densities, arrival times, muon counts where available, Cherenkov/fluorescence signals if present). The physical interpretation of O depends on three unknowns: (i) the primary energy E, (ii) the primary mass number A, and (iii) the hadronic interaction model H that governs the cascade development at energies beyond those calibrated by terrestrial accelerators. The forward map (E, A, H) ↦ distribution of O is subject to large intrinsic shower-to-shower fluctuations, and for most array geometries no observable is uniquely sensitive to A.

Formulate and answer the following inverse problem: design an estimation procedure that, from an ensemble of events with observables {O_i}, simultaneously reconstructs the primary energy spectrum dN/dE, the elemental composition (fractional abundances of mass groups), and constrains the hadronic interaction model H, in such a way that the recovered triple is not merely a self-consistent choice among trial models but is identifiable up to quantified uncertainty. In particular:

1. Give conditions on the observable set O and on the family of admissible hadronic models H under which the map (dN/dE, composition, H) → law of O is injective (identifiability).
2. In the absence of such conditions, characterize the degeneracy manifold of parameter combinations producing indistinguishable observable distributions, and provide a procedure to detect non-uniqueness when multiple combinations fit the data equally well.
3. Quantify the effect of intrinsic shower fluctuations on the achievable resolution in E and A for a given array configuration.
artifact.status_search_result: The disentanglement of primary energy, mass, and hadronic interaction modeling in air-shower array data remains an acknowledged open problem in ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray physics. Recent reviews and experiments (Pierre Auger, IceCube/IceTop, LHAASO, KASCADE-Grande follow-ups) continue to report unresolved tensions (e.g. the muon deficit problem) and pursue multi-observable and machine-learning approaches, but no model-independent reconstruction has been established.

status_evidence.title: The Muon Puzzle in cosmic-ray induced air showers
status_evidence.snippet: Discrepancies between predicted and measured muon numbers in extensive air showers signal limits of hadronic interaction models and complicate mass composition inference.
status_evidence.claim: The energy/mass/hadronic-model degeneracy is unresolved and actively studied.

status_evidence.title: Pierre Auger Collaboration, mass composition results
status_evidence.snippet: Mass composition inferences depend on the choice of hadronic interaction model; different models yield different composition fits.
